name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,338

entries.clue: Stressed oarsman turned up in prison (8)

indicatorNotes.turned up: in a down entry, turning a word up reads it from bottom to top
indicatorNotes.in: the rower is placed inside the prison

blocks.note: the can is slang for prison

annotation.surface: A rower is jailed and feels the strain.
annotation.walkthrough: "Stressed oarsman" reads as one tired rower, but stressed is the definition on its own; "turned up" only works because this is a down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone careworn shows the strain of long worry, which is what being stressed looks like.

blocks.note: the nautical name for one side of a ship, facing forward

annotation.surface: A ship has sailed from harbour.
annotation.walkthrough: "Port" looks like a harbour noun; here it is the nautical word for the left-hand side.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the past tense of leave means departed, and sailors call the left side of a vessel port.

entries.clue: Warning about tax curbing entrepreneurship initially (6)

indicatorNotes.about: CA, short for circa, means about
indicatorNotes.curbing: to curb is to restrain, and the tax restrains the E by closing round it
indicatorNotes.initially: initially means at the start, so take the first letter of entrepreneurship

annotation.surface: A cautionary word that taxes stifle small business.
annotation.walkthrough: "About" looks like a link to the topic of the warning, but it is the abbreviation CA; VAT is the British sales tax.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym borrowed from Latin 'let him beware': a caveat is a formal warning or proviso.

entries.clue: Put in a bid for boat (6)

blocks.note: formally offer a price for a contract
a small boat serving a larger ship

annotation.surface: Someone bids at auction for a boat.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one action, bidding to buy a boat; really the two halves each define the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: firms tender for contracts by submitting bids, and a tender is the small boat that ferries supplies to a ship.

entries.clue: Smoke joint with Mike for hours (8)

indicatorNotes.for: Mike stands in for the hours: M replaces H

annotation.surface: Someone smokes a joint with a pal called Mike for hours.
annotation.walkthrough: The joint is a shoulder, not a cannabis cigarette; swap its H for M.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: a fire that smoulders burns slowly, giving off smoke without flame.

entries.clue: Daredevil right on top of tree (4)

indicatorNotes.on top of: in a down entry, R sits above ASH

annotation.surface: A daredevil climbs to the top of a tree.
annotation.walkthrough: "Daredevil" is used as an adjective here, as in a daredevil stunt, so it matches the answer's part of speech.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: daredevil as an adjective describes reckless boldness, which is what a rash act shows.

annotation.surface: A textile mill is told to cut its production speed.
annotation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as the phrase "lace rate", the speed at which lace is produced; the question mark flags the whimsy.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to lacerate is to tear the flesh with a jagged cut, as a slash does.

blocks.note: the sum divided by the count

annotation.surface: A middling miser.
annotation.walkthrough: Tight means stingy with money, not closely fitting.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: someone tight with money is ungenerous, and in statistics the average of a set is its arithmetic middle value.

blocks.note: a golf tee supports the ball

annotation.surface: A bench that a whole group leans on for support.
annotation.walkthrough: The support is a golf tee, the peg that holds up the ball.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a settee is an upholstered sofa, one kind of seat.

indicatorNotes.for auditor: an auditor is a listener, so the note is heard, not read

blocks.note: doh is the first note of the sol-fa scale

annotation.surface: Money is hidden inside a note for the accountant.
annotation.walkthrough: An auditor in the surface checks accounts; here it is simply someone who hears.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang: the word for bread dough became informal for money, much as bread itself did.

entries.clue: Porter perhaps primarily at lodge entrance (3)

indicatorNotes.primarily: primarily means first of all, so take the first letter of each following word

blocks.note: first letters of At, Lodge, Entrance

annotation.surface: The porter stationed at the lodge entrance, as at a college.
annotation.walkthrough: The porter looks like a doorman, fitting the lodge; it is a dark beer, and "perhaps" marks it as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: porter, the dark London beer, is one variety of the answer, hence "perhaps".

annotation.surface: Someone too busy is failing to make time for things.
annotation.walkthrough: "Make time" reads as a set phrase; split it, making FORGE and time T.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to neglect a duty is to leave it undone, as if it had slipped the mind.

annotation.surface: A string of praise for a book or film.
annotation.walkthrough: The list looks like three synonyms, but only the last is the definition; ripping is dated British slang for splendid.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a thriller that holds your attention tight is both thrilling and exciting.

entries.clue: Water down colour puce, losing power (6)

indicatorNotes.losing: puce loses P, the abbreviation for power

annotation.surface: Diluting puce paint makes it paler.
annotation.walkthrough: Puce looks like the colour in question, but the colour is RED and puce is only raw letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the figurative sense: watering down a plan or a drink lessens its strength.

entries.clue: What char does caught bending over (8)

annotation.surface: A cleaning lady is caught bent over at work.
annotation.walkthrough: A char, or charwoman, is a British word for a woman paid to clean houses, not the fish or burning.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the whole phrase describes a charwoman's job, housework for hire.

entries.clue: Comes back from the dead, seemingly in frilly knickers? (6)

annotation.definition2: Comes back from the dead, seemingly

blocks.clueFragment: Comes back from the dead, seemingly
blocks.note: a made-up verb: reverse the act of dying with the prefix UN

annotation.surface: A ghost returns wearing frilly knickers.
annotation.walkthrough: Split the answer as UN-DIES: if dying is dies, coming back to life would be un-dies; "seemingly" admits it is not a real word.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: frilly knickers are one kind of the informal underwear word, and the invented verb un-die would mean return to life.

blocks.note: a lorry is British for a truck

annotation.surface: A pedestrian knocked down by a little lorry.
annotation.walkthrough: A lorry is the British word for a truck.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense: strike means hit, so its past form matches hit read as past.

indicatorNotes.Devious: devious means crooked, so the letters are twisted

annotation.surface: A crossword compiler's tricky methods.
annotation.walkthrough: "Setter's way" reads as the compiler's style; the 's is merely possessive glue and way is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a way is any road or path, as in Appian Way, and a town road is one kind.

entries.clue: Looking intently but missing a thread (6)

indicatorNotes.missing: missing means lacking, so the word goes without the A that follows

annotation.surface: Someone peers closely but still can't find the thread.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone losing track of a plot; the thread is a literal strand of fibre.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are thin twisted cords of fibre, differing only in thickness.

annotation.surface: Doing sums on behalf of a toddler.
annotation.walkthrough: The verb, usually followed by up, is British for totalling a column of figures.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a short form of total used as a verb for adding up, and an old word for a very young child.

entries.clue: One spiteful traveller returning after six (5)

indicatorNotes.returning: the traveller's word goes back to front
indicatorNotes.after: the reversed REP comes after VI

annotation.surface: A spiteful salesman comes home after six o'clock.
annotation.walkthrough: The traveller is a commercial traveller, a sales REP; the snake's name is also used for a treacherous, spiteful person.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: calling someone a snake-like name paints them as venomous, a spiteful person.

annotation.surface: Arguing against someone's opinion.
annotation.walkthrough: "Contend with" reads as a phrase meaning cope with; split it, and W is the standard abbreviation for with.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: your view on a matter is the way you see it, that is, your opinion.

entries.clue: New split engulfing Church of England (6)

indicatorNotes.engulfing: to engulf is to swallow whole, so the split closes round CE

annotation.surface: A fresh schism swallows up the Anglican church.
annotation.walkthrough: The split is a rent, a tear or rip, not a schism.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something that happened lately, not long ago, is new.

indicatorNotes.checking: to check is to hold back, and the cow holds H in by surrounding it

annotation.surface: A dairy supplier inspects hospital meals.
annotation.walkthrough: "Milk supplier" sounds like a dairy firm; it is simply a cow.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal slang: originally pidgin English, the word is now casual American for grub or food.

indicatorNotes.cut by: the hen is cut open and W is put in

annotation.surface: A wife carves up a chicken in the kitchen.
annotation.walkthrough: "Chopped chicken" reads as one phrase; chopped is the definition and chicken the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as a past participle: timber cut with an axe has been chopped, as in rough-hewn logs.

blocks.note: abbreviation for the British Conservative party
to found is to set up

annotation.surface: The Tory party springs a surprise campaign launch.
annotation.walkthrough: CON is short for Conservative, one of Britain's main parties; to found something is to launch it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to astonish someone by defying their expectations is to surprise them.
